title: Migrate from LLaMA-Factory to Soup CLI
description: Migrate from LLaMA-Factory to Soup CLI with one command. Field mapping, side-by-side config example, and reasons to switch.

blocks.html:
Migrate from LLaMA-Factory to Soup CLI

Switching from LLaMA-Factory to Soup CLI takes one command. Soup CLI offers a simpler YAML schema, 2–5× faster training via Unsloth, and a unified CLI for training, serving, and export.

One-line migration

This produces a soup.yaml file equivalent to your LLaMA-Factory config, mapping:

LLaMA-FactorySoup CLI
model_name_or_pathbase (a root-level string, not base.model)
stagetask: sft gives sft, pt gives pretrain, rm gives reward_model, and dpo, kto and ppo keep their names
finetuning_type: loratraining.lora.r (LoRA is on when r > 0)
finetuning_type: fulltraining.lora.r: 0 and training.quantization: none, a full fine-tune. Only stage: sft can do this: any other stage exits 1
lora_ranktraining.lora.r
lora_alphatraining.lora.alpha
quantization_bittraining.quantization: 4 gives 4bit, 8 gives 8bit; with quantization_method: hqq it gives hqq:Nbit (N of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8), with eetq it gives eetq (8 only). No quantization_bit gives none
pref_loss (read only under stage: dpo)task: sigmoid gives dpo, and ipo, orpo and simpo give the task of the same name. Any other value exits 1
pref_betatraining.dpo_beta for dpo, training.kto_beta for kto, training.orpo_beta for orpo, and training.ipo_tau under pref_loss: ipo (since v0.77.0). Under pref_loss: simpo it has no Soup equivalent and is dropped with a warning
simpo_gammatraining.simpo_gamma, under pref_loss: simpo only (since v0.77.0)
lora_targettraining.lora.target_modules: all, or no lora_target at all (LLaMA-Factory's default), gives all-linear; a comma-separated list becomes a list (since v0.77.0; through v0.76.1 it gave auto, which adapts two of the seven projections on Llama)
val_sizedata.val_split, and 0 when the key is absent, because LLaMA-Factory trains on every row by default (since v0.77.0; through v0.76.1 the split was dropped and Soup's default of 0.1 applied)
datasetdata.train: ./<dataset>.jsonl. The name is a LLaMA-Factory registry entry, so point it at the real file
per_device_train_batch_sizetraining.batch_size
cutoff_lendata.max_length (sequence length lives under data)
templatenothing: Soup auto-detects the chat template from the tokenizer. Override with data.chat_template if you need to pin one.

If lora_rank or lora_alpha is missing from the source, the importer writes LLaMA-Factory's own defaults since v0.77.0: r: 8, and alpha of twice the rank (#1807, #1901). Through v0.76.1 it wrote Soup's r: 64 and alpha: 16. Every source key the importer does not map is now listed in one warning (1 LLaMA-Factory key(s) not migrated (no Soup equivalent, or not read by soup migrate): do_train for the example below). A finetuning_type of freeze or oft has no Soup equivalent: the importer warns and writes LoRA.

Side-by-side example

LLaMA-Factory config:

blocks.code:
model_name_or_path: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stage: sft
do_train: true
finetuning_type: lora
lora_rank: 16
lora_alpha: 32
dataset: alpaca_en
template: llama3
cutoff_len: 2048
per_device_train_batch_size: 2
gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
learning_rate: 2.0e-4
num_train_epochs: 3

blocks.html: Soup CLI equivalent (soup migrate itself writes format: auto, val_split: 0.0, target_modules: all-linear, quantization: none and no backend line, warns that alpaca_en is a LLaMA-Factory registry name, and lists do_train as not migrated; backend: unsloth and format: alpaca below are hand-written):

blocks.code:
base: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
task: sft
backend: unsloth            # root-level, NOT under training

data:
  train: ./alpaca_en.jsonl  # LLaMA-Factory dataset names are registry entries; point at the real file
  format: alpaca
  max_length: 2048          # sequence length lives under data
  val_split: 0.0            # the source has no val_size: LLaMA-Factory trains on every row

training:
  quantization: none        # the source has no quantization_bit; Soup's default would be 4-bit QLoRA
  epochs: 3
  lr: 2.0e-4                # the key is lr, not learning_rate
  batch_size: 2
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
  lora:
    r: 16                   # LoRA turns on when r > 0; there is no enabled flag
    alpha: 32
    target_modules: all-linear   # the source has no lora_target, which means all

blocks.html:
With backend: unsloth, add training.gradient_checkpointing: true if you want Unsloth's checkpointing: since v0.77.0 the Unsloth backend honours the key, and the default false turns checkpointing off (#1981).

To freeze layers, note that since v0.77.0 training.freeze_layers and freeze_ratio reach a LoRA run (a frozen layer gets no adapter, #2145) on backend: transformers only (with backend: unsloth, as above, they are refused at load), and they need a list of lora.target_modules: the string all-linear the importer writes is refused when the model is built, so replace it with [q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj]. Through v0.76.1 the freeze did nothing on a LoRA run.

Why migrate?

  • Faster training — backend: unsloth gives 2–5× speedup on Llama/Qwen/Gemma/Mistral
  • Single YAML schema validated by Pydantic v2 (no silent typos)
  • Unified CLI — soup train, soup chat, soup eval, soup serve, soup export all in one tool
  • 171 ready-made recipes — soup recipes list
  • Built-in GGUF/Ollama export
  • Dry-run migration — preview the config with --dry-run before writing

Dry-run preview

Prints the converted config to stdout without writing. Without --dry-run, soup migrate writes soup.yaml in the current directory (--output picks another path) and asks before it overwrites a file that exists (--yes skips the question). It checks the result with Soup's own config loader before writing, so the file it hands back loads.

Then run soup doctor --config soup.yaml to see the loader's errors and warnings for the result. Its list of settings it knows to be unread is short, so a clean report is not a guarantee that every key takes effect.

If you migrated before v0.77.0

Regenerate and diff (#1807, #1901). Through v0.76.1 the importer:

  • dropped val_size, so Soup's val_split: 0.1 held out a tenth of the rows where LLaMA-Factory trains on every row by default;
  • wrote r: 64, alpha: 16 for a source without lora_rank or lora_alpha, where LLaMA-Factory trains r: 8 at alpha 16;
  • turned lora_target: all, and a missing lora_target, into target_modules: auto, two of the seven projections on Llama;
  • dropped pref_beta under pref_loss: ipo.

If you migrated before v0.76.0

Check the soup.yaml you generated, because the importer changed what it writes. Upstream's changelog lists three results that were wrong:

  • An unquantized source wrote no quantization line, so Soup loaded it as 4-bit QLoRA, and a full fine-tune source got LoRA r=64 instead of a full fine-tune (#1215, #1302).
  • stage: dpo with pref_loss: ipo became task: dpo. A pref_loss of hinge, kto_pair or any other value became task: dpo with no warning; it now exits 1 and names the value (#1214, #1560).
  • pref_loss: orpo or simpo under a stage other than dpo became task: orpo or task: simpo; LLaMA-Factory reads pref_loss only under stage: dpo, so the stage's own task is kept now.

If your source was bf16 or a full fine-tune, or used one of those losses, the run you got may not have been the run you meant. Regenerate and diff. The same applies to Axolotl and Unsloth sources, see Migration.
